card: Moves the getblocktemplate RPC template cache from function-local static variables into BlockTemplateManager. This eliminates hidden process-scoped state that can leave dangling CBlockIndex pointers across multiple node contexts in tests, enforces compile-time thread safety under cs_main, and adds unit tests for template invalidation rules. The refactor advances the BlockTemplateManager tracking issue #33758 and unblocks #36357.
changed_since_previous: Initial full patch provided; no structural divergence from the previous description.
evidence: Author description cites tracking issue #33758: 'This addresses the getblocktemplate part of the "Remove remaining global states" TODO in #33758, as suggested in #35675 review.'
Author description notes concrete failure mode in tests: 'cached CBlockIndex* can outlive the ChainstateManager that owns it when a process creates more than one node context (as the unit tests do)'.
problem: getblocktemplate caches block templates using process-scoped function-local statics. Because of this global lifetime, cached raw CBlockIndex pointers can outlive the ChainstateManager in multi-node test environments, locking requirements are not verified at compile time, and the caching and invalidation logic cannot be directly unit tested.

risk.why: A flaw in template refresh logic could cause miners calling getblocktemplate to construct blocks on a stale tip, producing invalid blocks and lost hashpower.

summary: Moves the getblocktemplate template cache from function-local statics into BlockTemplateManager. The cache is encapsulated in the node context, protected by cs_main with Clang thread-safety annotations, and references block tips by hash rather than storing raw CBlockIndex pointers. It also adds unit test coverage for cache rebuild rules and failure recovery.
